Coercion and safe action

Select each stage to understand why a safety-first response protects people, families and critical telecommunications operations.

Why this matters:

Before you respond: keep safety first

Pressure may focus on a person, a family member or an important work role. This activity shows the pattern at a high level so that you can recognise concern, avoid acting alone and use trusted support.

Summary: the safe response is never solo

Tiger kidnapping relies on pressure and isolation. Do not try to resolve a threatening situation by yourself, debate the caller, or work around an established control.

Practical takeaway: Prioritise immediate safety, use the organisation’s emergency and security contacts through a trusted channel, and let trained responders coordinate next steps.
